title: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics (Version 2, 03/26)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly changing evidence base on whether generative AI tools improve mathematics learning. Because large language models and related tools are evolving faster than conventional reviews can be completed, the authors propose and maintain LLAMA LIMA, a versioned living meta-analysis designed to be updated regularly as new studies appear.

The approach is a living systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA-LSR guidance. The authors searched SCOPUS and preprint sources for experimental and quasi-experimental studies of generative AI interventions in mathematics education, including studies where the intervention used generative AI and the control group did not. Version 2 includes 21 studies, 38 effect sizes, and 4,071 participants. The included studies span multiple educational levels, including primary, secondary, undergraduate, and adult learners, and cover a range of generative AI purposes such as tutoring, assessment and feedback, instruction, mathematical problem solving, collaborative-learning support, and teacher support.

The authors estimate effects using a Bayesian multilevel meta-analytic model to account for multiple effect sizes nested within studies and cumulative evidence updating. The pooled effect of generative AI interventions on mathematics learning is positive but uncertain, with Hedges’ g = 0.42 and a 95% credible interval of [0.13, 0.72]. Publication-bias analysis using RoBMA found weak evidence against publication bias, although the bias-adjusted model-averaged effect was somewhat smaller.

The paper concludes that generative AI may support mathematics learning, but the current evidence base remains limited and heterogeneous. The authors emphasize that effects are not yet robust enough for broad generalization and likely depend on instructional design, learner characteristics, context, and implementation. Future versions are planned to add moderator analyses as more studies become available.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems, including large language models and AI chatbots, used as instructional interventions to support mathematics learning through purposes such as tutoring, feedback, explanation, solution generation, and learning support.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper synthesized experimental and quasi-experimental studies in which generative AI was used in instructional interventions for mathematics learning, compared with control groups that did not use generative AI.

findings.finding_summary: Across 21 studies contributing 38 effect sizes and data from 4,071 participants, generative AI–based instructional interventions had a positive pooled effect on mathematics learning outcomes (Hedges’ g = 0.42, 95% credible interval [0.13, 0.72]). The authors report substantial between-study heterogeneity (study-level SD = 0.28, 95% CrI [0.01, 0.67]) and additional within-study variability (SD = 0.71, 95% CrI [0.52, 0.96]), indicating that effects varied considerably across contexts.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a living meta-analysis following PRISMA-LSR with Bayesian multilevel modeling and publication-bias assessment, but it is an arXiv preprint that has not undergone formal peer review. The evidence base is still limited, heterogeneous, and includes some preprints, so the synthesis has some concerns despite a rigorous methodology.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled meta-analytic effect on mathematics learning outcomes was positive and above the medium-impact threshold (g=0.42, 95% credible interval [0.13, 0.72]). The authors note substantial uncertainty and heterogeneity, but the estimated average effect is >=0.20.
